title: Ask Linux to write text
summary: Assembly: Ask Linux to write text. Change Hi to Hey and change the length to 4.
introduction: The write system call uses rax=1, rdi=1 for standard output, an address in rsi and a length in rdx.
learningObjectives: Ask Linux to write text with Assembly
Change Hi to Hey and change the length to 4

blocks.text: On x86-64 Linux, save lesson.asm. Run nasm -f elf64 lesson.asm -o lesson.o, then ld lesson.o -o lesson. Run ./lesson, then printf 'exit code: %s\n' "$?" immediately.

blocks.title: Ask Linux to write text
blocks.code:
global _start
section .data
message: db "Hi", 10
section .text
_start:
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    lea rsi, [rel message]
    mov rdx, 3
    syscall
    mov rdi, 0
    mov rax, 60
    syscall

blocks.text: The data contains two letters and one newline byte. Linux writes three bytes, then exits with zero.
Change Hi to Hey and change the length to 4.

blocks.title: Watch out
blocks.text: The length counts bytes, including the newline byte.
